clue.text: Source of raw fish found outside the channel

indicators.note: found outside says the fish sits around the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its opening letter is used

explanation.surface: A fisherman explains where the fresh catch came from: just beyond the shipping lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' takes R from 'raw'; 'found outside' puts TENCH around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trench is a long narrow ditch, a kind of channel dug in the ground.

clue.text: Volumes shown by millions in digits

indicators.note: in places the millions letter inside the word for digits

parts.note: toes are the digits of the foot
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Books selling in the millions, the sales figures shown in numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digits' looks like numerals, but here it means toes; 'in' puts M inside TOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomes are large heavy books, and a volume is one book.

clue.text: Worms discovered in one-masted ship

indicators.note: ship is read as a verb, to send off, so these letters are dispatched into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Worms are found in the timbers of a small single-masted sailing vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ship' looks like part of the picture of a sailing boat, but it is the anagram signal working on the nine letters of 'one-masted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, a large group of unsegmented worms.

clue.text: Male right to start baling mature vegetation

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, which is all that is taken

parts.note: to age is to mature or grow old

explanation.surface: A farmer claims his right to begin baling once the crop is ripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' takes B from 'baling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is grass and other herbaceous plants, green growth generally.

clue.text: Drink the newspapers stamp down on

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
the press is the collective name for newspapers

explanation.surface: A drinker vows to crack down on the tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppress something is to quash or crush it, forcibly keep it from showing.

clue.text: Photographer's studio used for firing practice?

explanation.surface: A photographer's studio doubles as a place for target shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: Photographers 'shoot' pictures, so the studio where they work is a gallery for shooting; the question mark flags this playful first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer takes shots in a studio, a gallery for shooting; a shooting gallery is also a range where people fire at targets.

clue.text: Ran through recipe for cooking deer's head

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked up into something new, the way a recipe is cooked
the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Instructions for preparing a deer's head as a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' turns RECIPE into PIERCE; 'head' takes D from 'deer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pierced is to be stabbed or run through, as by a sword.

clue.text: Fit to support English queen, being placid

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other, so it comes after it

parts.note: fit means able, as in fit to do a job

explanation.surface: A loyal subject is fit to support the English queen, staying calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' sets ABLE beneath EQU in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Equable means even-tempered and calm, never easily upset.

clue.text: Suspect a torch bearing witness

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so these words carry the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A suspect carries a torch at a crime scene, watched by an onlooker.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'suSPECT A TORch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is an onlooker, someone who sees an event as it happens.

clue.text: Grumble that two odds are reversed

indicators.note: are reversed tells us to read the doubled word from right to left
two means the word for an odd thing is written twice

parts.note: rum means odd or peculiar, so two odd things are two rums

explanation.surface: A complaint that a pair of betting prices have been swapped round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles RUM; 'are reversed' turns RUMRUM back to front. 'Odds' looks like betting prices, but each odd is the adjective rum (strange).
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low complaint, the sort of muttered discontent people voice.

clue.text: Finished making true advance

parts.note: over means finished, as in the game is over

indicators.note: making suggests the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Having finished, the speaker turns a promise into reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' rearranges TRUE into TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an approach or opening move, a friendly advance made to someone.

clue.text: Take away underground?

explanation.surface: A lesson in sums, or a description of land below the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as SUB TRACT, the word reads as a tract (area of land) that is sub (below), hence underground; the question mark flags this whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to deduct one number from another; a sub-tract, read playfully, is a stretch of land lying below.

clue.text: Groom a troop leader for battle

parts.note: to groom hair is to comb it

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A soldier is smartened up for the fight by his troop commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes T from 'troop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is fighting between armed forces, a synonym for battle.

clue.text: Just a little fly swallowed by the boy

indicators.note: swallowed by means the insect ends up inside the other word

parts.note: a son is a boy, someone's male child
a midge is a tiny two-winged fly

explanation.surface: A small boy has accidentally swallowed a tiny insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' could be a verb, but here it is the insect noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A smidgeon is a very small amount, a tiny bit.

clue.text: Little Augustus rose, mysterious, seeing a source of sweetness

indicators.note: rose means went up, and in a down clue going up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: Gus is a short form of the name Augustus
arcane means secret or mysterious

explanation.surface: A child named Augustus stood up, puzzled, after spotting something sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns GUS upward to SUG in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is the tall grass whose juice is refined into table sugar.

clue.text: Shortcoming in desert?

explanation.surface: A flaw shown up in a dry wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun, the sandy waste, but it is the verb: to defect is to desert a cause or country.
explanation.definitionFit: A defect is a fault or imperfection; to defect is to abandon one side and join another.

clue.text: Disposable weapons?

parts.note: disposable is read not as throwaway but as at one's disposal, so the clue means the armaments a force has available to use

explanation.surface: Throwaway arms, used once and binned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposable' suggests single-use items; read it as available for use.
explanation.definitionFit: Firepower is the destructive capacity of the guns and missiles a force can deploy.

clue.text: Leave Sunday drink and natter

parts.note: to go is to leave
to sip is to drink in small amounts

explanation.surface: Someone goes out on a Sunday for a drink and a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle talk or chatter about others, much like a natter.

clue.text: How one might launder fake coins and rings?

parts.note: a sham is a fake or counterfeit
p (pence) stands for small coins in British money
O is ring-shaped, so two rings give two Os

explanation.surface: A crook wonders how to clean counterfeit coins and jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launder' hints at laundering dirty money, but the answer is a cleaning product for hair or carpets.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a liquid detergent used to wash hair or clean carpets.

clue.text: Play on words — dig individual language!

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
a jab is a poke or dig
I, the Roman numeral one, stands for individual or single

explanation.surface: A joke at someone's expense: wordplay, a personal dig, in a single tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the Indo-Aryan tongue spoken in the Punjab of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Good bowling — no runs for the boss!

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricket captain praises a tidy spell of bowling that conceded nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six deliveries from one bowler, and runs are the points scored.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor is a person in charge, a head of an organisation or region.

clue.text: Victory is firm — America is sticky!

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for victory, as in V for Victory
taken as written
Co. is the abbreviation for company, a firm
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A triumphant declaration that the American win is assured.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscous describes a thick, glutinous liquid that resists flowing.

clue.text: An explanation from engineers when working

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
as can mean when, as in as I left
on means working, as with a machine switched on

explanation.surface: Engineers give an account of why the machine is running.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A reason is a cause or justification, something that accounts for what happened.

clue.text: Final job and call for retirement

parts.note: last means final
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Someone's final job before they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Last Post is the bugle call sounded in British military bases at nightfall and at funerals; 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Last Post is a bugle call that signals the end of the day, when soldiers retire to their quarters.

clue.text: Links across Germany offering daily highs and lows

indicators.note: across means the links stretch over the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: ties are links or bonds
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Connections across Germany yield rises and falls in the daily figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts TIES around D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides rise and fall twice daily, giving high and low water.

clue.text: H is like a buccaneer

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a buccaneer is a pirate

explanation.surface: Someone called H is compared to a pirate.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter H stands for a breathy sound; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirate is the breathed sound of h, so the letter itself is called one.

clue.text: Where a nurse works in advance

explanation.surface: A nurse working on a hospital ward, ahead of the patients.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ON WARD, it says where a nurse works; as one word it means forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse works on a ward of a hospital; onward means moving ahead or forward.

clue.text: Hostility encompassing alternative to an atrocity

indicators.note: encompassing means surrounding, so the hostility word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: enmity is hostility or ill will
or introduces an alternative, as in this or that

explanation.surface: Hostility with an alternative to all-out cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link, and 'alternative' is the conjunction that offers a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: An enormity is a grave crime or wicked act, an outrage.

clue.text: Remains to cover resistance from vagrants

indicators.note: to cover means the remains word is wrapped over the other letter

parts.note: stays means remains, as in she stays at home
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Remains are used to hide resistance by homeless wanderers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' puts STAYS around R; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strays are wanderers with no home, such as lost animals or vagrants.
